metadata.summary: A multi-center intensive care unit database with records from 200,859 ICU admissions from 139,367 unique patients at 208 hospitals in the United States between 2014 and 2015. Includes vital signs, care plan documentation, medications, laboratory measurements, and severity of illness scores.
metadata.purpose: To support collaborative multi-center research, external validation, and federated learning of clinical models.

papers.title: eICU Collaborative Research Database, a freely available multi-center database for critical care research

ethics.privacy_measures: Data de-identified per HIPAA Safe Harbor standards; no protected health information retained.
ethics.legal_compliance: Compliant with HIPAA and US IRB regulations; data use restricted to non-commercial research.

extraction.notes: Baseline card derived solely from dataset_catalog.xlsx real metadata; remaining fields require paper/README or manual completion.
pending_verification: The following LLM fields were auto-dropped for violating schema constraints and reverted to baseline; pending manual review: annotation_type, medical_fields[list-items]

known_limitations: Limited to US hospitals participating in the Philips eICU program — may not represent global or underserved ICU settings.
Temporal restriction to 2014–2015 — may not reflect current practices, devices, or coding standards.
No explicit reporting of demographic subgroups (age, sex, race/ethnicity), limiting bias analysis.
Potential selection bias: hospitals self-select into eICU program; patients lack direct consent.
bias_and_limitations.modifications: Yes — data were de-identified, standardized, and mapped to common ontologies (e.g., LOINC, RxNorm); severity scores computed algorithmically.
bias_and_limitations.representativeness_concerns: US-centric, 208 hospitals — overrepresents large, tech-enabled academic and community ICUs; underrepresents rural, safety-net, and non-eICU-participating centers.
bias_and_limitations.generalizability_statement: Designed for multi-center generalization and external validation within similar US ICU settings; limited generalizability to non-US, pediatric-only, or resource-limited ICUs.
bias_and_limitations.subgroup_coverage: Subgroup coverage (e.g., by race, ethnicity, socioeconomic status) is not reported.
bias_and_limitations.missing_data: Missingness patterns not quantified in abstract; known incompleteness in free-text fields and optional documentation.

data_origin.selection_rationale: Records selected from the Philips eICU program, representing ICU admissions across participating US hospitals to enable multi-center critical care research.
data_origin.sampling_strategy: Consecutive ICU admissions from 208 US hospitals between 2014 and 2015; no explicit sampling (e.g., random/stratified) stated — appears to be census-like within participating sites.
data_origin.aggregation_multisource: Aggregated from de-identified EHR data across 208 geographically distributed US hospitals using standardized extraction pipelines.

population.target_population: Adult and pediatric ICU patients admitted to participating US hospitals between 2014 and 2015.
population.inclusion_criteria: ICU admission at a participating hospital within the Philips eICU program during 2014–2015.
population.exclusion_criteria: Patients not admitted to an ICU or outside the program’s coverage period and geography.
population.missing_groups: No explicit reporting of underrepresented groups; abstract states 'no explicit demographic subgroup statistics'.

annotation.annotation_method: Derived from structured and semi-structured EHR fields (e.g., vitals, labs, medications, APACHE severity scores); no human annotation per sample.
annotation.labeling_provenance: Clinical data extracted and curated from Philips eICU platform EHR feeds.

benchmarks: eICU Benchmark (e.g., mortality prediction, length-of-stay estimation)
tasks_and_use.excluded_tasks: Real-time clinical decision support; commercial deployment; direct patient identification or re-identification.
